history.summary: The cheapest psf in the batch ($1,118) for a huge 1163 sqft 2BR at $1.3M, ~6% under the $1,185.5 URA median, with a future CRL Serangoon North station 920m away. Far East/Sino build with decent reviews. But it's 26 years old (~73 yrs lease) — the lease-decay and financing question caps it at Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: Value is the whole thesis: $1,118 psf and a 1163 sqft footprint give the lowest entry-cost-per-sqft here, below the $1,185.5 median, and the 7.6% resale CAGR (131 txns) is well-supported. CRL Serangoon North (CR9, 920m) is a genuine future catalyst and Far East/Sino is a reputable builder with 7.1/10 resident ratings. The counterweight is age — built 2000, ~73 years of lease left and accelerating decay, which weakens financing for future buyers and is the main reason resale liquidity could thin over a 5-7yr hold. Big and cheap, but the lease clock and dated fittings keep it balanced.

history.rating_rationale: Attractive entry: $1.39M for a 1,152 sqft 3BR keeps the buyer pool wide and the PSF (1206) is roughly at the URA median (1185.5). 7.6%/yr resale CAGR on 131 txns is strong, and CR9 Serangoon North (Cross Island Line, ~2030) is a genuine within-1km catalyst. history.summary: The 06-09 Avoid rested on "ask is at the $1,167 market average" — but that was the size-pooled average (mixing 1,500+ sqft low-psf units). Against the correct same-size cohort (1,151-1,162 sqft, 12-mo median ~$1,198 psf, 9 prints), the $1,118 ask is a genuine ~6-7% discount, so the strongest validated forward signal (cheap-vs-peers in OCR; D19 realized fwd +3.7%/yr) does fire — and the backtest shows cheap old OCR leaseholds outperformed, contradicting the lease-decay narrative. But the cohort band spans $1,066-$1,258 (±9%) including a Mar 2026 print BELOW the ask, so the discount sits inside cohort noise; with <10% of forward variance explainable, this is a near-tie, not an edge — Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: Upgrade from Avoid: the prior at-market claim was a size-pooling error — $1,118 psf is ~6-7% below the same-size 12-mo median (~$1,198, n=9), a real verified discount in the best forward region (OCR), with deep liquidity (580 units, 131 URA txns), low $1.3M quantum, and a dated CR9 Serangoon North catalyst (2030, 920m) inside the 5-7yr hold. Held back from Buy: the discount is modest and within the cohort's ±9% dispersion (Mar 2026 printed $1,066 — below the ask), the CR9 walk is marginal at 11 min, ~69-yr lease (~63 at exit) narrows the late buyer pool, and no en-bloc prospect.

history.summary: A 1,152 sqft 3BR at Regentville (D19 Hougang, 99yr from 1996, 69yr left) scraped at $1.28M / $1,111 psf — an ask that sits BELOW every one of the project's 31 same-size-band URA prints of the last 24 months ($1,146-$1,259 psf for the 1,152 type) while five sibling listings of the identical unit type, from five other agents, sit live at $1.35M-$1.50M. The size is real and deeply traded, so this is not a sqft mis-scrape — but an unverifiable outlier ask is not value. On its own market rather than the district median, the honest read is ~-7% vs 12-month same-size comps if $1.28M is transactable, and ~0% if the true clearing ask is the $1.35M the same unit type is otherwise offered at. Sound OCR fundamentals, spent re-rating, thin carry: Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: The algo's 855 is a verdict on Regentville-vs-D19, not on this ask: re-scoring the identical unit at $1.42M still returns 709, so $140k of price is worth only ~57 points. The score's two largest positives are the two my research discounts. (1) age_value 16.5 comes from -23.7% vs the age-adjusted D19 median, but that median blends Serangoon/Sengkang/Punggol stock sitting on rail; Regentville has no operational MRT (920m to CR9 Serangoon North, U/C to ~2030 — realsmart's own note is 'plan for a bus ride or drive'), and MRT proximity is a measured as-of-T negative (std_B -0.11) while future-infra has no measured forward power. Against its OWN market the discount is ~7%, not 24%. (2) appreciation 10.8 rests on a trailing 7.59%/yr CAGR that is real and not a size-mix artifact (realsmart median PSF $784 in 2021 -> $1,174 in 2026, +8.4%/yr on PSF medians, so mix-robust) — but that IS the 2021-26 OCR bull re-rating old leaseholds, which per the backtest carries ~0 forward power. Buying now is buying after that trade has run, not into it. What genuinely fires: OCR region (realized fwd +3.7%/yr, the best region), very deep liquidity (580 units, 1,393 lifetime txns, 31 same-size prints in 24mo, buyer_pool std_B +0.16), a low $1.28-1.35M quantum into a 67%-HDB-buyer pool, and Rosyth School at 352m — a real family-demand anchor for a 3BR. What holds it down: realsmart REALSCORE 3.7/5 with only 71.5% profitable — 235 of 819 computable exits LOST money on a deep sample, against an average holding period of 9.2yrs that is LONGER than the 5-7yr hold being underwritten; 3.8% gross / 2.3% net yield (realsmart independently estimates 3.7%) is thin carry; lease at ~62-63yrs on exit; and six concurrent listings of this exact unit type means the buyer's own exit is into a crowded queue. Neutral is robust to how the price question resolves: if $1.28M is transactable on an ordinary unit it is a ~7% discount inside a cohort band that itself spans +/-5%, i.e. noise given the model explains <10% of forward variance; if it is a teaser or an inferior (low-floor/unrenovated) unit, the true ask is $1.35M+ and the discount vanishes entirely. Both paths land at or below Neutral, so no Buy — but the fundamentals are too sound for an Avoid.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Solid but thin. realsmart's latest 12 contracts median $4,000/mo, with 3BR contracts of this size band at $3,500-$4,300 — independently confirming the $4,100 model rent (rent_source ura_project_bed, conf 0.95). 50 rental contracts in the past month across the project is genuinely deep tenant demand, helped by Rosyth School and Hougang town amenities. But $4,100 on $1.28M is 3.84% gross / 2.32% net (realsmart's own estimate: 3.7%), which is ordinary carry — and it gets worse, not better, if the true entry is $1.35M+ (3.6% gross). No MRT within walking distance caps the expat/professional tenant segment; this rents to families, at family prices. Note the prior also runs the other way: high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth (std_B -0.16), so a mid-3s yield is neutral, not a warning.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Underwrite ~4%/yr, not the data's 7.59%. The trailing number is real and mix-robust — realsmart's annual median PSF series runs $752 (2019) -> $784 (2021) -> $1,174 (2026), so this is genuine PSF re-rating, not the shoebox-mix artifact seen elsewhere. But it is the 2021-26 OCR bull revaluing cheap old leaseholds, a regime effect with ~0 measured forward power, and the +56% since 2019 means that trade has largely been run. The forward case rests on the measured levers: OCR region (+3.7%/yr realized), a modest cheap-vs-peers discount, and deep buyer-pool depth — against a live MRT-distance negative and a lease grinding from 69 to ~62yrs across the hold. That nets to roughly the D19/OCR baseline of 4.0-4.2%/yr, which is what I have overridden the rate to. The downside evidence is the sobering part: realsmart records 235 loss-making exits out of 819 here (71.5% profitable, REALSCORE 3.7/5) — this project has demonstrably lost owners money before, most likely 2008-2013 buyers exiting into 2014-2019, and the average profitable hold ran 9.2yrs, longer than the 5-7yr window.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Unknown, and that is a material gap. The listing carries no floor, stack, facing or unit number, and Regentville has no researched profile yet (stack_profile: not_researched), so no join is possible — running /research-development would not resolve it either, because there is no stack identifier on the listing to join against. What the prints do show is that Regentville has real floor/format tiering: within the same 1050-1400 size band, the 1,163 sqft type printed $999-$1,067 psf on four occasions and EVERY one was floor 01-05, while the 1,152 sqft type printed $1,146-$1,259 across floors 01-15. So a genuine low-floor discount at this project is worth roughly 5-8%, not the 13-17% gap this ask shows to its live siblings. The most probable physical explanations for a real $1,111 ask are a floor 01-05 unit in original 2000-vintage condition, or a poor facing/blocked outlook — any of which would justify the price rather than represent a bargain.
